verses.1: And in that place, the crowd gathered around him. They heard the words of God, and he himself became one with the lake Genesarate.
verses.2: And he saw two ships near the lake. The fishermen who were on those ships cleaned the nets.
verses.3: He then entered one of the ships, which belonged to Simon. He asked him to go back to his own land for a short time. After sitting down on the ship, he taught the people there.
verses.4: And when he stopped talking, he said to Simon: “He has brought you back down to the depths, and your networks have been destroyed.”
verses.5: And Simon replied, “Epiστάτα, since we spent the entire night cutting them down, we won’t be able to get anything from them. But on your behalf, I will destroy their networks.”
verses.6: And after doing this, they caught a large amount of fish. They also managed to unravel their networks.
verses.7: And they also caught those who were on the other ship, as they came to pick them up. Then they arrived, and both ships were damaged, so that they had to be sunk.
verses.8: When Simon Peter saw Jesus at the cross, he stepped forward and said, “Get away from me, Lord! I am a sinner.”
verses.9: For the net had enclosed him, as well as all those who were with him, in the field of fish that they had caught.
verses.10: Similarly, also Jacob and John were sons of Zebedaeus. They were companions of Simon. Jesus said to Simon, “Do not fear. From now on, people will live in peace.”
verses.11: And as they brought the ships onto land, everyone followed them.
verses.12: And it happened that, while he was in one of the cities, he saw a man who was completely covered in dirt. When he saw Jesus falling on his face, he asked him, “Lord, if you want, I can cleanse you.”
verses.13: And he stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I want you to be cleansed.” Immediately, the leprosy left him.
verses.14: And he also told him not to say anything. Instead, he should go and show himself to the priest. Then he should be cleansed according to what Moses commanded them.
verses.15: Moreover, more and more people began to listen to his words. Many people gathered together to hear him and to be healed from their illnesses.
verses.16: He, however, remained humble in the deserts, and prayed constantly.
verses.17: And one day, he also taught. There were Pharisees and teachers who had come from all over Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was sufficient for him to teach them.
verses.18: And they saw men carrying a man who was injured onto the bench. They tried to get him inside and heal him before his eyes.
verses.19: And not finding anyone who could carry him through the crowd, they carried him onto the stage through the doors. They placed him with the cross in front of Jesus.
verses.20: And seeing their faith, he said, “Man, let go of your sins.”
verses.21: And the scribes and the Pharisees began to argue with each other, saying, “Who is this person who speaks such slanderous words? Who can commit any sins, if not only God himself?”
verses.22: But Jesus, after hearing their discussions, said to them, “What are you discussing in your hearts?”
verses.23: What is more beneficial to say? Either “Forgive your sins,” or “Let go of them.”
verses.24: “So that you may know that the son of man has power over the earth to punish those who commit sins,” he said to the lost person. “I say, go back home with your suffering.”
verses.25: And a servant stood before them. Then, after he had done what was required of him, he went back to his master’s house, praising the God.
verses.26: And they were all terrified, and they praised the god. They were filled with fear, saying, “We know now that it’s truly incredible.”
verses.27: And after that, he went out and examined the ladder, named Leuin. He sat down on top of the ladder and said to him, “Follow me.”
verses.28: And everyone who remained behind followed him.
verses.29: And Levi made a large tent for him in his house. There was also a large crowd of people who ate with him, along with others who were also there.
verses.30: And the Pharisees and their scribes said to him, “Why do you eat and drink with sinners?”
verses.31: And when Jesus spoke to them, he said, “It is not necessary for those who are sick to seek a doctor. It is better for those who are healthy to do so.”
verses.32: I did not let the righteous be called sinners, but rather, I sent them into repentance.
verses.33: And they said to him, “The disciples of John fast and perform various rituals. The same is true for the Pharisees. But you, you eat and drink.”
verses.34: And he said to them, “Should not you be able to make the sons of the nymphs fast, since the nymph is with them.”
verses.35: But there will be days when the nymphs will not come. And when that happens, they will fast during those days.
verses.36: He also made a metaphorical comparison to them, saying that no new fold of fabric can be applied to an old garment. And if it does happen, then the fold from the new fabric won’t match the shape of the old garment.
verses.37: And no one pours fresh wine into old containers. But if someone does so, then the fresh wine will destroy those old containers. In that case, both the wine and the containers will be destroyed.
verses.38: But I want to drink fresh wine for the new athletes.
verses.39: And no one who drinks old wine wants new wine. For the old wine is still useful.
